signals.evidence: Asaf Langalben, head of Upper Galilee Regional Council: 'We will not agree to continue living under the threat of missiles over our heads'

Ramat Gan mayor Carmel Shama Hacohen announced to residents: 'Home Front Command informed me that as of this evening Ramat Gan returns to green status, meaning no restrictions. Full routine including Mimouna celebrations'
Ramat Gan mayor later clarified: 'There is no ceasefire with Lebanon yet, and Home Front Command has not announced any easing of emergency status'

Kfar Saba mayor Rafi Saer announced: 'Tomorrow morning the education system in Kfar Saba returns to full activity. Kindergartens, elementary schools, middle and high schools are all ready and prepared'

Shiba hospital operated in underground conditions for 40 days: lack of daylight, overcrowding, poor ventilation, and increased risk of infection spread. A tuberculosis patient exposed nearly 2,000 hospital staff and approximately 750 patients including 300 infants

Moshe Davidowitz, head of Matte Asher Regional Council: 'If the war against Hezbollah stops, this is a first-class value, moral and security failure. To stop now in Lebanon is to tell the residents of the contact line: your lives will now always be war'

Asaf Langalben, Upper Galilee Regional Council head: 'We are not interested in American ceasefires or opening the Strait of Hormuz. We are interested in one thing - dismantling the threat to Israel from Lebanon and rehabilitating the north'

Eyal Shuali, Kfar Vardim council head: 'We, the heads of the contact line authorities, are in fog regarding the Lebanon front. From Northern Command we were told the ceasefire does not include the Lebanon front'

Nurse at Ichilov Hospital: 'We waited a month and a half for daylight. It was suffering when we were forced to go underground. Patients who could walk had to descend two floors in crowding with every alert. It was a catastrophe'
Hospitals managed to maintain continuity of care despite operating in underground conditions for six weeks, with rapid adaptation to security reality

Ministry of Health: During Operation 'Lion's Roar' (Feb 28 - Apr 8, 2026), 7,433 casualties were hospitalized, with 116 currently admitted. Of these: 2,738 injured en route to shelter (4 severe, 73 moderate, 2,644 mild, 16 anxiety casualties)

IDF spokesperson: Clash between Palestinians and Israeli civilians in Kafr Taysir village, Manasseh, involving stone-throwing. One Israeli citizen and one Palestinian were injured and evacuated for medical treatment
Red alert sirens activated in Margliot and Manara communities on the Galilee Finger. Residents instructed to enter protected spaces immediately and remain according to Home Front Command guidelines

Ramat Gan mayor Carmel Shama Hacohen wrote to residents: 'Home Front Command informed me that as of this evening the city returns to green status - meaning no restrictions, full routine including Mimouna celebrations'

Kiryat Ono mayor Michal Rozenshteyn announced: 'Home Front Command updated me on transition to green policy from noon, allowing activities without special restrictions and without need for proximity to protected space'
Missile from Iran fell in Kiryat Herzog neighborhood, Bnei Brak at 3 AM, embedded in ground without detonating. If it had exploded, it could have caused severe damage to three nearby buildings

Resident of evacuated building: 'At 4 AM they started knocking on doors and taking people out. One of the things that bothered us most was that they didn't explain exactly what was happening - there was chaos, too many forces and too little information'

Resident criticized evacuation scope: 'They evacuated residents living in the front of the building who were not in the danger zone at all. Families with children were taken out of their homes unnecessarily'
Gur Hasidic court announced resumption of studies for the first time on Isru Chag, with the Admor instructing the chief supervisor to open all yeshivas for three hours of study.

Despite ceasefire with Iran, uncertainty exists about school reopening; Education Ministry did not provide guidance for this scenario; schools and kindergartens unlikely to open, requiring preparation time.
Absence of government guidance creates uncertainty among parents, students, and teachers; most schools and kindergartens unlikely to open; system requires preparation time for resuming studies.
Tel Aviv, Ramat Gan, Ramat HaSharon, and Raanana announced preparations to resume studies from Thursday; Raanana awaiting Home Front Command guidance before acting.

Home Front Command permits resumption of studies in most of the country; 16 municipalities and regional councils announced resumption of studies including Tel Aviv, Herzliya, Givatayim, Kfar Saba, Ramat Gan, and others.

Local Government Center chairman Chaim Bibas: 'Education system will open in a differential manner, granting each local authority head autonomy to decide on opening pace according to field team readiness.'
Light rail in Gush Dan will return to full operations starting Thursday at 07:00 following ceasefire with Iran. Nine underground stations that served as protected spaces during war will reopen.

Education Minister Yoav Kisch instructed resumption of in-person learning in education institutions starting Thursday in accordance with Home Front Command defense policy and 'green' designated communities.

Education Ministry emphasized emotional support for students, identification of needs, and adapted return plans; will allow institutions to open at pace of local authority readiness and field constraints.

Israel Airports Authority announced immediate easing of restrictions at Ben Gurion Airport starting midnight; duty-free shops and related services will reopen; Herzliya Airport resumes Thursday; Ramon Airport resumes Sunday.
El Al announced return to extensive operations starting next week, operating full-aircraft flights to approximately 30 destinations including European, Middle Eastern, and long-haul routes.

Red Crescent Society reported 2,503 casualties over 40 days of war: 26 deaths, 29 serious injuries, 50 moderate injuries, 1,812 light injuries, and 586 panic and shock cases. Direct missile injuries: 594 people including 23 deaths.

Red alert sounded in northern Israel including Haifa at 3 a.m. on April 8 without advance warning; rocket fire from Iran recorded. This was the fourth Iranian rocket attack after Trump's ceasefire announcement.

NETA and Tevel companies announced light rail in Gush Dan will resume full operations Thursday, April 9 at 07:00. Underground stations of the red line that functioned as bomb shelters during war will reopen.

IDF called on Lebanese civilians in Tyre to evacuate immediately; Israeli strikes reported in southern Lebanon by Lebanese media; Prime Minister Netanyahu's office stated two-week ceasefire does not cover Lebanon.
Israeli carrier Arkia announced preparation for gradual expansion of flight operations at Ben Gurion Airport following ceasefire with Iran; expects to resume regular flight schedule starting May 3.

IDF stated no changes yet to Home Front Command guidelines despite ceasefire; military holding ongoing assessments and discussions on policy changes; no decision made; public will be updated when changes occur.

Israeli carrier Israir announced preparation to expand flight operations; expects to gradually increase flight frequencies and passenger numbers; plans flights to Athens, Larnaca, Budapest, Tbilisi, Batumi, Rome, Berlin, and Rhodes.

Hungarian airline Wizz Air extended suspension of flights to and from Israel through April 27, extending from previously announced April 20 date. Israel's airspace shut to foreign airlines since February 28.
Sirens sounded in northern border city Kiryat Shmona and surrounding towns warning of rocket fire from Lebanon; potentially first Hezbollah attack since ceasefire announcement.

Israel expected to announce plan for full return of flight operations at Ben Gurion Airport from midnight Wednesday-Thursday following ceasefire. Transportation Ministry announcement expected Wednesday evening.

Arkia announced flights to Athens, Larnaca, Rome, Vienna, London, Amsterdam, Paris, Bangkok, New York, and Budapest. Israir announced flights to Athens, Larnaca, Budapest, Tbilisi, Batumi, Rome, Berlin, and Rhodes.

Transportation Ministry announced Israel will fully reopen airspace and resume regular operations at Ben Gurion Airport starting midnight. Herzliya Airport resumes Friday; Ramon Airport resumes Sunday; Haifa Airport return considered end of week.

El Al announced return to regular schedule by gradually increasing flight frequencies from Ben Gurion. From midnight, El Al will operate departing flights at full passenger capacity. Starting next week, El Al plans flights to 30 destinations.
Police preparing to reopen holy sites in Jerusalem's Old City for prayer and public gatherings tomorrow in light of two-week ceasefire.

Schools across Israel will reopen and resume normal functioning for first time since February 28. In northern Israel near Lebanon border, some restrictions remain; educational activities permitted only in bomb shelters.
Home Front Command released updated guidelines effective Thursday morning; schools will open in most of country with gathering limits canceled; restrictions remain in Lebanon border areas.

Lebanon's health ministry reported Israeli strikes killed 182 people and wounded 890 on Wednesday; total since March 2: 1,739 killed and 5,873 wounded. Toll does not distinguish combatants from civilians.

Municipalities including Emek Hefer, Lev Hasharon, Kadima-Zoran, and Tel Mond announced kindergartens and schools reopening in line with safety requirements. Ramat Gan, Kfar Saba, Herzliya, Hod Hasharon, Mevaseret Zion preparing to resume classes.

Education officials emphasized gradual return with focus on emotional support, social reintegration, and safety preparedness drills rather than full academic routines. Hybrid learning models combining in-person and remote learning expected.

Sirens sounded in northern Israel Wednesday afternoon after Hezbollah fired rockets from Lebanon. Fragment from intercepted rocket fell in open area causing no injuries. Sirens in Kiryat Shmona identified as false alarms.

IDF Home Front Command released update to guidelines Wednesday; starting 6 a.m. Thursday, schools will open in most of country with gathering limits canceled. In areas near Lebanon border, current guidelines remain unchanged.

Most Tel Aviv apartments lack safe rooms or building shelters despite high rents. Residents evacuated from damaged buildings gathered belongings for hotels; others walked with children near neighborhood shelters.
Lebanese Health Ministry reported 8 killed and 28 wounded in Israeli strike on cafe in Sidon. Hezbollah-affiliated Al-Mayadeen reported 2 killed in strike on car in Ras el-Ayn area.

Israel Airports Authority conducting ongoing assessments and examining expansion of operations at facilities in accordance with security directives and Transportation Ministry. Arkia expects rise in departing passengers; preparing to expand schedule by May 2.

Main obstacle to expanding flights at Ben Gurion Airport is U.S. military presence; airport serves as joint U.S.-Israeli military airfield hosting mainly U.S. refueling planes parked in spaces needed for civilian aircraft.
Lebanese Red Cross reported Israeli strikes killed and wounded more than 300 people in Beirut and southern suburbs (Dahiyeh). Many reportedly trapped under rubble; hospitals under heavy strain.

Israeli tech executives and families seeking flights and evacuation routes; Ben Gurion departures hall nearly empty during Passover. Ron family experienced multiple sirens during departure process; journey to US via Madrid took extensive time.

Gal Shor, SVP of operations at Lightrun: 'We reached a point where we bought 10 tickets per person just to create some chance someone would get out. People left four days early with three exhausting connections just to attend a three-day conference.'

Home Front Command has not yet updated guidelines after Iran ceasefire; conducting ongoing assessments. Local authorities awaiting official changes expected later. Some mayors moved ahead prematurely; Ramat Gan mayor initially announced full return then clarified no changes approved.

Designer Geller: 'With the way the country has been run over the past three years, I immediately knew that if I didn't take care of myself, I wouldn't have a safety net from any official body.' Municipal representative told him: 'My condolences. This is not a property tax matter. Good luck.'

Home Front Command lifted wartime restrictions starting 6 a.m. Thursday. Local authorities moving to resume full activity; many planning to reopen schools, cultural institutions, and public services. Tel Aviv and surrounding cities announced return of all education frameworks.
Netanyahu addressing public: 'When you showed resilience and sat in safe rooms and shelters, together we achieved tremendous accomplishments -- our fighters at the front and you on the home front.'

42 killed in 40 days of fighting in Operation Roaring Lion: Yaakov Bitton (16), Avigail Bitton (15), Sarah Bitton (13), Ronit Elimelech (45), Sarah Elimelech (71), Oren Katz (46), Yosef Cohen (41), Bruria Gloria Cohen (76), Gavriel Revah (16).

Mother of Staff Sgt. Touvel Yosef Lifshiz: 'We haven't slept for months. I don't know what sleep is, because Touvel knew he could call at any hour, and I would answer. I waited for the phone to ring, just to hear that he was okay.'

Mother of Staff Sgt. Lifshiz: 'Our lives were turned upside down. We did not expect this. That morning, we were told everything was fine.' Five other soldiers wounded in incident; one officer seriously injured.
Staff Sergeant Touvel Yosef Lifshiz, aged 20, fell during combat in southern Lebanon. Five additional combat soldiers were injured to varying degrees and evacuated to hospital.

Tel Aviv authorities announced activities will resume tomorrow starting at 10:00 a.m., including after-school programs. Givatayim announced return to studies tomorrow with schools opening at 9:00 a.m. and kindergartens at 9:30 a.m. Rishon LeZion announced studies will resume tomorrow starting at 8:00 a.m., including after-school programs.

Carmel Shama-Hacohen, Mayor of Ramat Gan, informed residents that Home Front Command classified Ramat Gan as 'green status, meaning no restrictions. Full routine.' Mayor of Hod Hasharon announced city is 'preparing for as full a reopening of the education system as possible.'
Netanyahu: 'When you proved resilience and sat in the protected rooms and shelters, together, we achieved incredible achievements; our soldiers on the front, and you at the rear.'
El Al announced resuming broad and significant operations and accelerating return to regular flight schedule, with flights to 30+ destinations resuming as early as next week.

Jerusalem education system will fully resume operations starting tomorrow (Thursday, April 9), with classes beginning at 08:00 in all educational institutions across the city, including daycare centers. Afternoon programs will operate as usual.
Holy sites in Jerusalem will reopen to visitors and for prayer starting tomorrow morning, following updated instructions from Israel Home Front Command.

Jerusalem District Commander Avshalom Peled ordered increased operational deployment with hundreds of police officers, Border Police personnel, and volunteers deployed across the city, along main roads, in the Old City, and at holy sites.

One resident of a settlement point in the Jordan Valley was seriously wounded after a rock struck his head during an attack by an Arab mob. The injured man received initial treatment from Magen David Adom teams.
An Israeli civilian and a Palestinian civilian were injured during an incident in Tayasir involving rock-throwing and were evacuated to hospital for medical treatment.
